en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Saṅghādisesa Offenses
3. The Training Rule on Lewd Speech At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Udāyī was dwelling in the forest.
The dwelling of that venerable one was beautiful, lovely to behold, and pleasing.
Now at that time, a large number of women came to the monastery to inspect the dwellings.
Then those women approached the venerable Udāyī.
Having approached, they said this to the Venerable Udāyī:
“Venerable sir, we wish to see the dwelling of the Master.
Then the Venerable Udāyī, having shown those women the dwelling, [showed them] the path for excrement and the path for urine of those women.
He speaks both in praise and in dispraise; he begs and entreats, asks and cross-examines, instructs and advises, and even reviles.
Those women who are wanton, profligate, and shameless laugh with the Venerable Udāyin, converse with him, laugh loudly at him, and mock him.
But those women who were modest came out and complained to the bhikkhus:
“Venerable sirs, this is improper and unbecoming.
Even if our husbands had spoken to us in such a way, we would not have consented; how much less so by the venerable Udāyin?”
Those monks who were of few desires... [and so forth]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
"How can the Venerable Udāyī address a woman with indecent words?
Then those monks, having rebuked the Venerable Udāyī in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then, on this occasion and for this reason, the Blessed One had the community of monks assembled and questioned the Venerable Udāyin:
“Is it true, Udāyin, that you addressed a woman with indecent words?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him:
“It is unseemly, foolish man, it is unbecoming, it is improper, it is unworthy of a recluse, it is unallowable, and it is not to be done.
How indeed, foolish man, could you address a woman with indecent words?”
"Have I not, O foolish man, taught the Dhamma in many ways for the sake of dispassion and not for the sake of passion? ... [and so on] ...
the subsiding of the fever of sensual desire has been declared.
This, O foolish man, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence... [and so on]"
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:

“Whatever monk, having entered [upon a path] with a perverted mind, should address a woman with vulgar words, as a youth would a young woman, connected with sexual intercourse—that is a *saṅghādisesa*.
“Whatever monk” means:
Whoever is such ... [as previously described] ...
a bhikkhu ...
this is the kind of bhikkhu intended in this context.
"Immersed" means being lustful, having longing, and having a mind bound [to it].
"Altered" means...
A lustful mind is changed; a corrupt mind is changed; a deluded mind is changed.
However, in this context, it is a lustful mind that is intended by the term "changed.
As for the phrase "a woman":

A human woman, not a female spirit (yakkhinī), not a female ghost (petī), and not an animal. She must be intelligent and capable of discerning what is well-spoken and what is ill-spoken, and what is gross and what is not gross.
"Gross speech" refers to speech connected with the anus, the urinary tract, or sexual intercourse.
"To shine upon" is said to mean transgression;
as when [a man] shines upon a young woman.
A young man with a young woman, a youth with a youth, a sensual enjoyer with a sensual enjoyer.
"Connected with sexual intercourse" means associated with the practice of sexual intercourse.
"Saṅghādisesa": ... [as before] ...
for that reason also it is called "saṅghādisesa.
Taking two paths as his subject, he speaks praise, he speaks dispraise; he entreats, he entreats further; he questions, he questions further; he explains, he instructs; and he also reviles.
"To speak praise" means to extol, laud, and commend the two paths. "To speak dispraise" means... [the rest of the sentence is missing from the source text].
He reviles, mocks, and censures two people.
He begs, saying:
"Give to me; you ought to give to me."
He entreats, saying:
"When will your mother be pleased?
When will your father be pleased?"
"When will the deities be pleased with you?
When will there be a favorable moment, a favorable hour, and a favorable interval?
When shall I obtain union with you?"
She asks: "How do you give to your husband,
and how do you give to your lover?"
"To question" means:
"Is it really so that you give to your husband in this way,
and to your lover in that way?"
"To explain" means that, when asked, she says: "Give it in this way; by giving in this way, you will be dear and pleasing to your husband.
"To instruct" means...
When not asked, she says: "Give it like this; by giving in this way, you will be dear and pleasing to your husband.
She is said to revile him, saying:
"You are without signs!"
You have only the appearance [of a woman], you are bloodless,
and you are constantly bleeding.
You are a constant garment, you are flowing,
you are a crest-jewel.
You are a woman, you are a paṇḍaka,
you are a man-like woman,
you are one of confused gender.
"Regarding one who has both sexual organs": she is a woman, perceives herself as a woman, and is full of lust.
And a monk, with reference to the female organ or the urinary organ of that woman, speaks either in praise or in dispraise.
If he speaks, entreats, urges, questions, cross-examines, explains, instructs, or reviles [her],
it is an offense of Saṅghādisesa.
…pe…
If there are two women and he perceives them as two women, and he is lustful;
and if a bhikkhu, referring to the anus or the urinary tract of those two women, speaks both praise and dispraise … [and so on] … or even reviles them,
there is an offense of two *saṅghādisesas*.
... [as before] ... A woman and a paṇḍaka; perceiving both as women, and being lustful.
A bhikkhu, referring to the anus or the urinary tract of both, speaks in praise or speaks in dispraise ... [as before] ...
If he reviles her, there is an offense of wrongdoing (dukkaṭa) together with a formal meeting of the Saṅgha (saṅghādisesa).
…pe… And she is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.

If a bhikkhu, with reference to a woman’s body— excluding the path of excrement and the path of urine— from below the collarbone to above the knees, speaks in praise or speaks in dispraise … or even reviles her,
there is an offense of thullaccaya … [and so on] … [when] two women are present and he perceives them as two women, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, excluding the anus and the urinary tract of two women, speaks in praise or speaks in dispraise of the area below the collarbone and above the knees...
or even reviles them, there is an offense of two thullaccayas... [and so on].
If it is a woman and a paṇḍaka, and he perceives both as women, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, excluding the anus and the urinary tract, speaks in praise or speaks in dispraise of her body from below the collarbone down to above the knees, and he also reviles her,
there is an offense of thullaccaya for the [offense of] dukkaṭa …pe….
And she is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, referring to the area above the collarbone and below the knees of a woman, speaks in praise or speaks in dispraise of her … [and so on] … or even reviles her,
there is an offense of wrong-doing … [and so on] … Two women,
perceiving them as two women, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, referring to the area between the breasts and below the knees of two women, speaks in praise or speaks in dispraise of them … [and so on] … or even reviles them,
there is an offense of wrong-doing for both … [and so on] ….
If it is a woman and a paṇḍaka, and he perceives both as women, and he is lustful.
And if a bhikkhu, referring to both of them from above the collarbone down to below the knees, speaks in praise or speaks in dispraise … [and so on] … or even reviles them,
there is an offense of wrong-doing for both … [and so on] … If it is a woman,
he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, referring to a woman’s physical body, speaks either in praise or in dispraise of it … [and so on] … or even reviles her,
he commits an offense of wrong-doing … [and so on] … Two women,
perceiving them as two women, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, referring to something connected to the bodies of two women, speaks in praise of one and speaks in dispraise of the other … [and so on] … or even reviles them,
there is an offense of wrong-doing for both … [and so on] ….
If it is a woman and a paṇḍaka, and he perceives both as women, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, referring to something connected to the bodies of both [the woman and the man], speaks in praise or speaks in dispraise … or even reviles them,
there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas* … [and so on] … There is no offense—
One who has the welfare as the primary concern,
the Dhamma as the primary concern,
and the instruction as the primary concern.
"Of one who is insane, of a first-offender.
3.1. Summary Verse on the Subjects of Discipline.
Reddish-brown, strewn with gravel,
rough, long, and unevenly sown—
does the path not sink down?
"Faith through giving and action.
3.2. The Case of Discipline:
Now at that time, a certain woman was wearing a newly dyed woolen blanket.
A certain monk, being lustful, said this to that woman:
"There is blood on you, sister.
She did not understand.
“Yes, venerable sir, it is a new woolen blanket.
He became anxious, thinking, “A training rule has been laid down by the Blessed One; have I perhaps fallen into an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa)?
He reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“There is no offense, monk, against the *saṅghādisesa*;
there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
Now at that time, a certain woman was wearing a coarse woolen blanket.
A certain monk, being lustful, said this to that woman:
"Your pubic hair is coarse, sister.
She did not understand him.
“Yes, venerable sir, it was a coarse woolen blanket.
He became anxious... [as before] ...
“There is no offense, monk, for a *saṅghādisesa* offense.”
“There is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, a certain woman was wearing a woolen blanket that had not yet been washed.
A certain monk, filled with lust, said this to that woman:
“Sister, your hair is indeed matted,” he said.
She did not understand him.
“Yes, venerable sir, it is a new woolen blanket,” she replied.
He became anxious... [as before] ...
"There is no offense, monk, against the *saṅghādisesa*;
there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*)."
Now at that time, a certain woman was wearing a coarse woolen blanket.
A certain monk, filled with lust, said this to her:
"Your hair is coarse, sister."
She did not understand him and said, "Yes, venerable sir, it is a coarse woolen blanket.
He became anxious... [as before]...
“There is no offense, monk, against the *saṅghādisesa*;
there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
Now at that time, a certain woman was wearing a cloak.
A certain bhikkhu, being lustful, said this to that woman:
"Your pubic hair is long, sister.
She did not understand him.
“Venerable sir, it is a woolen cloak.
He felt remorse... [as before] ...
“There is no offense, monk, of *saṅghādisesa*.”
“There is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, a certain woman was returning after having had a field plowed.
A certain lustful monk said this to her:
“Sister, have you sown?
She did not understand.
“Yes, noble sir, but it has not yet sprouted.”
He became anxious... [as before] ...
"There is no offense, monk, against the *saṅghādisesa*;
there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*)."
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu, having seen a female wanderer coming along the opposite path, became lustful for her and said this to her:
“I hope, sister, the road is not sinking?
She did not understand.
“Yes, bhikkhu, you will practice [accordingly].
He became anxious... [as before] ...
“There is no offense, bhikkhu, of *saṅghādisesa*.”
“There is an offense of thullaccaya.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu, being lustful, said this to a certain woman:
“You have faith, sister.”
“Moreover, that which you give to your master, you do not give to us.
“What is it, venerable sir?
“Sexual intercourse.”
He became anxious... [as before] ...
"Bhikkhu, you have committed an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu, being lustful, said this to a certain woman:
“Sister, you have faith.
However, that which is the supreme gift—that we do not teach.
“What, venerable sir, is the supreme gift?”
“Sexual intercourse.
He became anxious... [as before] ...
“Bhikkhu, you have committed an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).”
Now at that time, a certain woman was working.
A certain monk, filled with lust, said to her:
"Stop, sister; I will do it. …pe…
“Sit down, sister; I shall do it,” he said. … “Lie down, sister; I shall do it.
But she did not understand.
He felt remorse... [as before] ...
"There is no offense, monk, against the *saṅghādisesa*;
there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*)."
The third training rule on indecent speech is concluded.
